Class 4 · Chapter 6 of 9

Timetables, dates and clock errors

Use intervals and distinguish the clock reading from the true time.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Measure and convert units. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find a missing time interval.
  • I can use a timetable or calendar.
  • I can correct a fast or slow clock.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

How long did it last?

A show starts at 8:45 and ends at 10:30.

8:45 to 9:00 is 15 minutes. 9:00 to 10:00 is 1 hour. 10:00 to 10:30 is 30 minutes.

Add them: 1 hour 45 minutes.

Screen 2 of 4

Read a timetable

A bus leaves at 9:40 and you are ready at 9:25.

Count on from 9:25 to 9:40.

You wait 15 minutes.

Screen 3 of 4

Use a calendar

Count days on a calendar. From 29 March to 8 April: 2 days to 31 March, then 8 more.

That is 10 days.

In March 2026 the 1st is a Sunday, so the 29th is a Sunday too.

Screen 4 of 4

Fast and slow clocks

A fast clock shows too much time, so take the gap away.

This clock shows 4:20 and is 15 minutes fast.

The true time is 4:05.

Words to know
interval
The time that passes between a start and an end.
timetable
A list that shows when things start, stop or leave.
fast clock
A clock that shows a later time than the true time.

For parents

What your child learns

The end time is the start time plus the length of the task. Add hours first, then minutes. If minutes pass 60, make a new hour. A timeline shows tasks one after another.

A common slip

Children often add minutes beyond 60 without carrying. When minutes reach 60, add 1 to the hour. Use a clock face to check.

5-minute home activity: Task timeline

  1. Plan 3 tasks, each with a length in minutes.
  2. Draw them as bars end to end.
  3. Start at 6:15 and add each length.
  4. Say when the work finishes.
